findings.text: - Section 7 proposes reckoning a declared window against the endpoint, citing only _flight_schema.py effective_input_window as "partly built", and never names reckon/crew/serving_origin.py check_serving_origin (an existing tested capability that resolves a lane's serving origin and probes it over HTTP at /v1/models, built under crew-runtime-positive-controls commit 9ea06319) nor reckon/crew/context_budget.py refusal_census (which derives the endpoint's real refusal boundary from recorded streams). WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes - REASON: without naming these, an implementer reads section 7 as open ground and rebuilds an endpoint read that already exists, the exact rebuild this item exists to prevent.

- Section 7's done-when describes a dispatch gate on the endpoint's true boundary, but that gate already has an owner: _context_fit_verdict at reckon/crew/routing.py:3213 gates a dispatch on the smaller of usable_input_window and effective_input_window, and effective_input_window is defined in reckon/_flight_schema.py:307 and reckon/schema/flight.yaml:535 as measured from what the lane's own endpoint refused via refusal_census. At HEAD nothing in the codebase populates effective_input_window from refusal_census; it is declared (480000 in the committed ledger) but never produced, which is exactly the "partly built but not shown to fire" gap section 7 names. The plan should extend refusal_census into effective_input_window and prove _context_fit_verdict refuses on the disagreement. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes - REASON: naming refusal_census and _context_fit_verdict as the owner turns section 7 from an open question into a concrete wiring-and-fire measure, and stops a second declared-versus-served check being built beside the context-fit guard that already runs.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass. The plan's new interface is a single Dialect method, read_account_surface, which hides credential load, credential expiry, the HTTPS transport and the strict parse behind one call returning the shared budget block, and keeps the failure funnel intact.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding. Section 7's done-when asks for a declared-versus-served check that fires on disagreement, but that gate already has an owner: _context_fit_verdict in reckon/crew/routing.py consumes effective_input_window, which is defined as measured from the endpoint's own refusals via refusal_census. The section should name that owner and wire it rather than leave the question open.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding. Section 7 proposes verifying the declared window against the lane's endpoint but names only effective_input_window in the flight schema; it never cites the two existing mechanisms that already reach that endpoint: reckon/crew/serving_origin.py check_serving_origin, and reckon/crew/context_budget.py refusal_census.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass. Section 3 states why the existing BudgetProbe exchange cannot be extended to carry the HTTP read, because its shape is a held-open-stdin argv plus a list of protocol requests. That is the justification this item requires.
